new_scholarship.name: Cusanuswerk Promotionsstipendium (Auswahlverfahren für Promovierende) — Cusanuswerk Doctoral Scholarship
new_scholarship.program_type: Foundation scholarship for doctoral candidates (church talent development body)
new_scholarship.duration: Maximum funding period three years and six months, with additional extension options in cases of illness, maternity protection periods and child-rearing.

new_scholarship.application_period: Two annual selection rounds for external applicants: Verfahren I-2027 (Anmeldeschluss 1 November 2026, decision March 2027) and Verfahren II-2027 (Anmeldeschluss 1 June 2027, decision October 2027).
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Outstanding academic performance, interdisciplinary interest, social responsibility and voluntary engagement, membership in the Catholic Church with a lived Christian faith, university entrance qualification, and admission to doctoral study at a recognised university.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applications undergo an internal review and a first pre-selection based on all submitted documents, which can take up to eight weeks; the final decision is then made by an interdisciplinary panel of university lecturers that also includes the Conference for Catholic University Chaplaincy (KHP) and the Cusanuswerk head office. Alumni of the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme have earlier internal deadlines (1 February for the spring round, 1 September for the autumn round).
new_scholarship.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who are members of the Catholic Church (or eligible Orthodox churches), already admitted to a doctorate at a recognised university, and seeking a parent-independent three-year stipend in Germany.
new_scholarship.description: The Cusanuswerk is the talent development body of the Catholic Church in Germany and funds doctoral candidates through its Promotionsförderung. The current round (Verfahren I-2027) accepts registrations until 1 November 2026 with a selection decision in March 2027. Funding is a parent-independent stipend of EUR 1,750 plus a EUR 100 research cost allowance, with optional health-insurance, child-care and family supplements and possible support for research stays abroad; the official page states no tuition-fee coverage. Foreign applicants must be admitted to a doctorate at a recognised university in Germany and prove German at C1, and applicants from developing or emerging countries are referred to the KAAD before applying to Cusanuswerk.
new_scholarship.notes: The official pages publish the doctoral funding details in German only; the German wording has been quoted rather than paraphrased.

programme_detail_official.description: The Cusanuswerk, the talent development body of the Catholic Church in Germany, runs an annual selection procedure for doctoral candidates in all subject areas. Applicants register online and upload an exposé of their doctoral project, evidence of academic performance and their personal career path by 1 November 2026 for the spring 2027 round. Selected candidates receive a parent-independent stipend of EUR 1,750 plus a EUR 100 research cost allowance for a maximum of three years and six months, with additional health-insurance, child-care and family supplements and possible support for research stays abroad.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Foundation scholarship for doctoral candidates (church talent development body)

For foreign applicants: assemble German C1 evidence (Goethe-Zertifikat C1/C2, DSH 2+, Test DaF 4/5, Telk C1 or UNICert III)
If you are from a developing or emerging country, contact KAAD first and get their confirmation before applying
Draft the exposé of your doctoral project — this is the core of the application
Arrange an academic teacher's reference (Hochschullehrergutachten) using the published template; the English template is available
Register in the OmniBuS portal early and upload everything well before 1 November 2026
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 November 2026 registration deadline — late registrations and late documents are explicitly excluded
Not being a member of the Catholic Church (or an eligible Orthodox church)
Foreign applicants whose doctorate is not at a recognised university in Germany, or who cannot evidence German at C1
Applying directly from a developing or emerging country without first having KAAD confirm ineligibility
Incomplete upload in OmniBuS by the deadline, including the academic teacher reference
estimated_uncovered_costs: No tuition-fee coverage is stated, so any doctoral tuition fees charged by your university are not covered by this award

new_scholarship.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany's largest and oldest scholarship foundation and funds about 14,000 students and doctoral candidates. Its doctoral scholarship pays a monthly stipend of EUR 1,650, with a research allowance of up to EUR 100 per year, a health-insurance contribution of up to EUR 100 per month, family and childcare allowances and separate travel grants. Applications are accepted only during published 14-day call windows — the current window runs 1 to 14 October 2026, with the selection meeting in May 2027 and the earliest possible scholarship start on 1 July 2027. The scholarship is not repayable.
new_scholarship.notes: Applications must be sent by post; the current call window closes on 14 October 2026, so this record is only useful for applicants able to dispatch documents immediately.

programme_detail_official.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes funds doctoral candidates throughout Germany with a non-repayable monthly stipend of EUR 1,650, a research allowance of up to EUR 100 per year, a health-insurance contribution of up to EUR 100 per month, family and childcare allowances and travel grants for research abroad. Following a sharp rise in applications since 2024, the foundation publishes short call windows roughly eight months before each selection meeting: 1–14 October 2026, 1–14 February 2027, 1–14 June 2027 and 1–14 October 2027. Complete application documents are sent by post, jointly with the doctoral supervisor.
